- Model consistently underestimates true price spikes, especially after sentiment shifts to positive (sentiment > 0.00) — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for such periods.
- After a sharp price spike (true > 75), model fails to capture continuation or overcorrects — apply lagged mean reversion: if true > 75 for 3+ days, forecast next day = prior true + 10% of prior true drop.
- When sentiment is low (0.00) and model is rising, it overestimates — cap forecast at 10% above recent 5-day average.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 70–65) after a spike, model often fails to anticipate — add 1–3% downward bias to forecast for 3-day horizon.
- Sentiment history with 0.20 or above correlates with higher true volatility — increase forecast variance by 10% for 30-day horizon if sentiment > 0.15.
- Model exhibits “overshoot” after spikes: if true peaks > 80, forecast often exceeds 85 — cap forecast at 85% of peak or 80 + 5% of prior true.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows mean reversion to 65–70 after 70+, apply 5–10% downward correction to forecast for next 5 days.
